more.def: A person or thing that keeps bothering you, especially in a small way.
examples: My little brother can be a pest when I am doing my homework.
The buzzing fly was a real pest during lunch.
Stop being a pest and let me finish my book.

easy.def: To keep bothering someone.
examples: Do not pester me.
The flies pestered us.
He pestered his sister.

more.def: To bother someone again and again, so that they get annoyed.
examples: Do not pester your sister while she is doing homework.
The mosquitoes pestered us all night.
The puppy pestered us for a snack.

easy.def: A poison used to kill bugs that harm plants.
examples: The farmer used pesticide.
Pesticide can hurt bees.
Do not touch pesticide.

more.def: A chemical that kills insects and other small animals that harm crops.
examples: The farmer sprayed pesticide on the apple trees.
Some pesticides can also harm bees and fish, so they must be used carefully.
Washing fruit helps remove any pesticide left on the skin.

easy.def: A green sauce made from basil.
examples: We ate pesto.
Pesto is green.
Pesto has basil.

more.def: A green sauce made from basil, nuts, cheese and oil.
examples: We tossed the pasta with pesto.
Pesto is made with fresh basil.
She spread pesto on the bread.

easy.def: An animal you keep at home.
examples: My pet is a cat.
Do you have a pet?
The dog is a good pet.

more.def: An animal that lives with people and is cared for by them.
examples: A hamster can be a good pet for a small apartment.
She feeds her pet fish every morning.
The class pet is a gentle guinea pig.

easy.def: To stroke an animal gently.
examples: I pet the dog.
She petted the cat.
Please pet the rabbit softly.

more.def: To touch an animal gently with your hand.
examples: The children petted the soft lambs at the farm.
He petted the horse's nose.
Cats purr when you pet them.

easy.def: One of the soft, colored parts of a flower.
examples: The rose has red petals.
A petal fell off.
I picked up a petal.

more.def: One of the soft, colored outer parts of a flower that surround its center.
examples: The daisy has white petals and a yellow center.
A single rose petal floated on the water.
The bright petals of the tulip opened in the morning sun.

easy.def: Small and slim.
examples: The girl is petite.
She is a petite lady.
She is petite.

more.def: Small and slim in size, usually said of a woman or girl.
examples: The petite girl stood on a box to reach the shelf.
She is petite, but she runs fast.
The dress was made for a petite person.

easy.def: A paper that many people sign to ask for a change.
examples: We signed a petition.
The petition asks for a new park.
The class made a petition.

more.def: A written request signed by many people that asks someone in charge to do something.
examples: We signed a petition asking for a new playground.
The class made a petition to keep the library open.
Hundreds of people put their names on the petition.

easy.def: A small sea bird.
examples: A petrel flew.
The petrel is a sea bird.
I saw a petrel.

more.def: A small sea bird that flies low over the waves, often far from land.
examples: A petrel skimmed the waves.
Petrels spend most of their lives at sea.
The petrel flew above the ocean.

easy.def: Too scared to move, or turned to stone.
examples: I was petrified of the dark.
The petrified wood is hard.
She stood petrified.

more.def: So frightened that you cannot move, or turned into stone over a very long time.
examples: She was petrified when she saw the huge spider.
We saw a petrified tree that had turned to stone over millions of years.
The mouse stood petrified as the cat came close.

easy.def: Oil from the ground.
examples: Petroleum is oil.
Gas comes from petroleum.
Petroleum is pumped.

more.def: A thick liquid found underground that is made into gasoline, oil and plastic.
examples: Gasoline is made from petroleum.
Oil rigs pump petroleum from the ground.
Petroleum is used to make plastic.

easy.def: A skirt worn under a dress.
examples: She wore a petticoat.
The petticoat was white.
The petticoat showed.

more.def: A light skirt worn under a dress or another skirt, especially in the past.
examples: She wore a white petticoat under her long dress.
In old times, girls wore petticoats to make their dresses puff out.
The lace of her petticoat peeked from under her skirt.

easy.def: Small and not important.
examples: It was a petty argument.
The petty problem was solved.
He got upset over petty things.

more.def: Small and not important, or mean about small things.
examples: They had a petty argument over a pencil.
Petty quarrels wasted their afternoon.
Do not waste time on petty problems.

easy.def: A garden flower with soft, trumpet-shaped blooms.
examples: Mom planted petunias.
The petunia is purple.
Petunias grow in pots.

more.def: A garden flower with soft, trumpet-shaped blooms in many colors, such as pink, purple and white.
examples: Mom planted pink petunias in the flower boxes outside the window.
The petunia has soft petals that look like small trumpets.
Bees buzzed around the purple petunias.

easy.def: A long bench in a church.
examples: We sat in a pew.
The pew is wooden.
She sat in the front pew.

more.def: A long wooden bench with a back, used for seating in a church.
examples: The family sat together in the front pew.
The wooden pew creaked when he sat down.
Rows of pews filled the hall.

easy.def: A soft gray metal.
examples: The cup is pewter.
Pewter is a gray metal.
A pewter plate.

more.def: A soft, silvery-gray metal made mostly of tin, used for cups and plates.
examples: The old pewter mug sat on the shelf.
Pewter is a mix of tin and other metals.
They ate from pewter plates.
